recipes.name: Dee's Dark Chocolate Granola
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons butter flavored spread (such as I Can't Believe It's Not Butter!® Spread)
0.25 cup sweetened dried cranberries (such as Craisins®)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a 9x13-inch baking dish with aluminum foil and spray with nonstick cooking spray.
Melt together the brown sugar, peanut butter, honey, butter flavored spread, and vanilla extract in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir until well combined; remove from heat.

Combine the oats, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl. Pour the brown sugar mixture into bowl; stir well to combine. Stir in the chocolate chips, dried cranberries, and almonds. Spoon into the prepared pan; pat down and spread evenly.
Bake in preheated oven until browned, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Dee's Dark Chocolate Granola
raw_recipe.description: This crunchy peanut butter and chocolate granola is great for breakfast, or any time that a chocolate craving hits.

review.reviewBody: This is absolutely amazing. I already have to make another batch. I made two changes: I used vegetable oil instead of butter spread, and added a tablespoon on cocoa powder for a little more chocolate. But I repeat, this is an amazing recipe.

This is a hit with my kids and grandkids! I changed the first batch by using orange honey, real butter, and sunflower seeds. The second batch I replaced the almonds with chopped walnuts, but kept the real butter and sunflower seeds. I used parchment paper on a large baking sheet and pressed the mixture down firmly with a big spatula. Once baked I let it cool completely before removing it from the pan. It comes out like peanut brittle, you just break off a pieces and store sealed in the refrigerator!! 
(Next time I may try Canola oil.)

I've made this several times and always forget to add the chocolate chips and dried cranberries. This time I added them after baking. I use coconut oil instead of butter spread and leave out the salt. We don't like salt in our granola (that we eat like cereal with milk). Besides what is on the ingredients list, this time I added toasted coconut, sunflower seeds, and chia seeds. Yummy! Sweeter than our usual though. It's also very good without the chocolate and cranberries!

Amazing. Used olive oil, and added 1 Tbsp cocoa powder to the dry mixture. Also left out the almonds and cranberries because I didn't have any. Just fabulous. Love it with milk. Stirred every five minutes, and it was done by 15 minutes. Will be making again. Thanks for sharing!

so easy, and so good! I doubled most ingredients except the brown sugar (used 3/4 c), and added an extra cups of oats when it looked like more "good stuff" than I wanted. Baked it 20 minutes, and added the chocolate chips after it cooled. Can't wait to try it on my instant pot yogurt in the morning

Very good. I used vegetable oil instead of butter spread and I baked the ingredients in the oven without the chips and cranberries. (Whenever I've made granola before and baked the cranberries in with the granola mix, I always end up scorching them which makes the granola taste terrible.) I just stirred in the cranberries and chocolate chips once the granola came out of the oven. I made sure to use a spatula to rotate the granola every five minutes so it cooked evenly. My kids had this in a yogurt/fruit breakfast sundae, I had this just in a bowl with FF milk. Good stuff. I'd make this again in a heartbeat.

I love this chocolate granola! A yummy treat, but pretty healthy as well! I always double it and cool for about 23 minutes total. I do add two tablespoons of cocoa powder to a double batch for a little extra chocolate flavor. And I use coconut oil in place of butter to make it a little healthier. Make sure you put parchment paper down or tinfoil on your pan for easy clean up!

Really good! I soaked my oatmeal for optimal nutrition so just had to change a few things. Doubled the recipe and soaked it in about 3/4 c. water with a generous splash of lemon juice and about 1 T. of whole wheat flour. Used sucanat in place of sugar (and used about 1/2 the amount) and real butter. Due to the soaking, I baked this at a low temp for about 45 minutes to crisp it up, and actually mistakenly almost burned it. We still enjoyed it, even extra toasty, and will add it to the breakfast rotation. Thanks!

This was my first attempt at making granola and it was fantastic! I made a few adjustments for my own nutritional preferences. I substituted coconut sugar, almond butter, and coconut oil. I added a couple of tablespoons of chia seeds and ground flax with the oats and a tablespoon of cocoa. Although I am not sure if the cocoa was necessary. Left out the cranberries and added mini semi sweet chocolate chips after it had cooled. This is going to be perfect on top of my Greek yogurt and berries.

We make this recipe quite often and now take a little creative license with it. I make the "sauce" but put in more dry ingredients which cuts back the sweetness. It was very good with ground flax sprinkled in it, fewer chocolates, and a variety of dried fruits. My son is allergic to nuts so I skip the almonds and add Kamut as the base. I've also used Agave Nectar when we're out of honey. When going to all the trouble make a double batch~ it freezes nicely.

Love this recipe! As soon as we run out I have to make another recipe. I tweak it for our preferences: I add 1 Tbsp add cocoa powder, decrease the brown sugar, and I crush the almonds finely (plus add a little extra). Great healthy breakfast to get my family going.
So good! maybe just a little less salt next time!

Very easy to make and delicious! I followed other suggestions...used butter instead of butter flavor spread; added Tblspoon of cocoa. Used a little water in the pan as the oat mixture did not get fully covered at first. I'll make this again!
This is my favorite granola recipe EVER! I've been using this recipe for years and it's always a hit. Thank you!
THIS IS FANTASTIC....I must admit I did double the chocolate chips and cranberries....I should have followed the advice of the other reviewers and doubled (or maybe tripled) it!
I love this recipe and how versatile it is. I've stopped buying packaged granola all together! Sometimes I use coconut oil in place of butter for a different flavor.
It turned out great! I would totally recommend this recipe. I just used white chocolate chips instead of brown chocolate chips which I like much better.

I am making these for the kids lunch. We have to be peanut free so I omitted the peanut butter and added 2 more tablespoons of honey. It is pretty sweet, but still very nice. Does anyone have any other suggestions?
I doubled the recipe and put the 2nd batch on a bigger tray, which meant cooking the granola in a thinner layer, which scorched it (word to the new granola makers like me).

My family & I love this!! All my friends ask for the recipe. It's great as is but I usually add a handful (1/8-1/4C) coconut, chia seeds, & wheat germ. This is great to eat when we're biking, hiking, etc.!
